findings.description: decompose-plan precedence order puts the explicit --overview-task-id CLI flag LAST after parent plan metadata and parent prd.json. Both Copilot and Codex flag this: a CLI override must win over discovered metadata, otherwise users cannot intentionally override stale embedded values. The doc inside the plan (§3.2 of the doc template) must reorder precedence so the flag is first.
findings.suggestedFix: Reorder the precedence list in the doc template's §3.2 to: (1) explicit --overview-task-id flag, (2) parent plan metadata block, (3) parent prd.json's overviewTaskId. Update both the doc template inside draft-plan.md and any acceptance criterion that depends on the order.
findings.resolution: Reordered §3.2 decompose-plan precedence list so the explicit --overview-task-id CLI flag comes first (highest precedence), then parent plan metadata, then parent prd.json. Updated the §8 acceptance criterion for decompose-plan and §9 tests to include a CLI-flag-wins precedence test, and added a top-level Acceptance Criterion pinning the new order.

findings.description: The doc tells convert-to-ralph-prd to read valid IDs from <repo_root>/plans/overview-data.js, but Ralph is a project-agnostic plugin and the same doc says elsewhere that 'the Ralph plugin doesn't know about overview-data.js'. Hardcoding a codexu-specific path conflicts with the plugin's design and will fail / misbehave in repos without that file. Make the lookup optional and config-driven, or fall back to a free-form prompt when the file is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: In the doc template's §3.1, reword the interactive prompt: 'If the repo has an overview-data file at a path discoverable via .ralph/overview-config.json (or any consumer-defined config), offer those IDs as a prompt convenience; otherwise prompt for a free-form string. Always allow skip / null.' Add a back-compat note that the prompt-list lookup is opt-in and the flag/free-form prompt is the canonical path.
findings.resolution: Reworded §3.1 to make --overview-task-id flag canonical, free-form prompt the default, and the overview-data.js lookup an opt-in config-driven convenience — no longer hardcodes the codexu-specific path.

findings.sectionRef: Research Findings > Technical Constraints (item 3) AND Files to Create/Modify > doc template §2
findings.description: Both Claude and Codex flag this: the plan claims 'both schemas use additionalProperties: true', but only prd-schema.json sets it explicitly (line 7). group-schema.json omits it, relying on JSON Schema's implicit default of true. The conclusion (non-breaking) holds, but the supporting fact is wrong and would mislead the future Ralph patch cycle when it audits the schemas.
findings.suggestedFix: In draft-plan.md, edit the Technical Constraints section AND the doc template's '§2 Ralph internals checked' to say: 'prd-schema.json explicitly sets additionalProperties: true (line 7); group-schema.json omits it, relying on JSON Schema default permissive behavior. Either way, adding the optional overviewTaskId field is non-breaking.'
findings.resolution: Corrected the inaccurate 'both schemas use additionalProperties: true' claim in the Codebase Context bullet and the doc template §2 to reflect that prd-schema.json sets it explicitly on line 7 while group-schema.json relies on the JSON Schema default.

findings.sectionRef: Acceptance Criteria (first bullet about section count)
findings.description: Both Copilot and Codex flag this: the AC says 'all 7 top-level sections' but then lists 10 (Context, Ralph internals checked, Patches required, Back-compat, Out of scope, Critical compatibility gotchas, Suggested landing order, Acceptance criteria, Tests, How to pick this up). An autonomous agent cannot verify '7' against a 10-item list.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the first acceptance criterion with: 'The doc contains all 10 top-level sections in this order: 1. Context, 2. Ralph internals checked, 3. Patches required (with subsections 3.1–3.4), 4. Back-compat, 5. Out of scope, 6. Critical compatibility gotchas, 7. Suggested landing order, 8. Acceptance criteria, 9. Tests, 10. How to pick this up.' Remove the parenthetical commentary about the source plan's '6 sections' typo from the criterion itself; keep it in plan prose if useful.
findings.resolution: Replaced the first AC bullet to say '10 top-level sections' with explicit numbered ordering (1. Context through 10. How to pick this up), and removed the parenthetical commentary about the source plan's '6 sections' typo.

findings.description: Both Copilot and Codex flag this: the AC says each of the 4 skill patches must include 'a schema-update directive', but brainstorm-with-ralph only updates an inline JSON example in its SKILL.md (no separate schema file), and plan-with-ralph has no schema update at all. The criterion is literally false for 2 of the 4 patches.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to: 'All 4 Ralph skill patches are documented. Each has a CLI flag (or prompt), a write location, and — where applicable — a schema or artifact-example update directive (prd-schema.json for convert-to-ralph-prd; group-schema.json for decompose-plan; SKILL.md JSON example for brainstorm-with-ralph; no schema change for plan-with-ralph).' Mirror the same precision in the doc template's §8 acceptance criteria list.

findings.sectionRef: Files to Create/Modify > doc template §6.1 AND §3
findings.description: §6.1 names patching skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md as one valid resolution (option A) for the YAML-front-matter compatibility issue. But §3 frames the future patch cycle as only 4 skill patches. If option A is taken, implement-with-ralph is a conditional 5th patch and must be named in the patches list so the future cycle doesn't miss it.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a §3.5 to the doc template titled 'Conditional patch: implement-with-ralph (if resolution A is chosen)' that points to skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md Phase 0 and specifies: skip leading --- YAML front-matter before applying the '# Implementation Plan:' first-line check. Cross-reference §6.1.

findings.sectionRef: Files to Create/Modify > doc template §3.4 and §6
findings.description: The doc suggests `yq eval` for YAML front-matter parsing, but Ralph's current prerequisite path only mandates jq (see ralph.sh prerequisites). If yq becomes a soft requirement, the future patch must update preflight and docs; alternatively the future patch could implement a shell-portable parser using jq + sed/awk over the YAML block.
findings.suggestedFix: In §3.4 and §6, change 'use yq eval' to 'use any shell-portable YAML front-matter parser (e.g., yq if added to plugin prerequisites; otherwise a sed/awk extractor that pipes the front-matter block to jq -R after YAML→JSON conversion). The future Ralph patch cycle decides which; if yq, also update the plugin preflight checks.'

findings.sectionRef: Files to Create/Modify > doc template §10 'How to pick this up' (the handoff command)
findings.description: The doc template uses POSIX-style forward-slash paths (e.g., D:/harness-efforts/codexu/plans/ralph-overview-task-id.md) in the verbatim handoff command. Existing repo docs and the source plan use Windows-style backslash paths (D:\...). On Windows-hosted bash the forward-slash form works, but for consistency and to match the contract in the source plan, the final command should use backslashes.
findings.suggestedFix: In the doc template's §10, change the handoff command path to `D:\harness-efforts\codexu\plans\ralph-overview-task-id.md`. Add a note that POSIX-style forward slashes also work on Windows-hosted bash but the canonical form in this repo is backslashes.

findings.sectionRef: Files to Create/Modify > doc template §7 Suggested landing order
findings.description: The landing order puts plan-with-ralph last (4), but decompose-plan (3) is instructed to read parent plan metadata whose format is decided by the plan-with-ralph metadata-block work AND the §6.1 resolution. If the future cycle follows the staged order literally, decompose-plan would implement against an unsettled metadata contract.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prerequisite note at the top of §7: 'Before any of the four staged skills land, the §6.1 metadata-format decision (front-matter vs HTML-comment block) MUST be settled — it determines the contract decompose-plan and plan-with-ralph both write/read.' Optionally restructure the order so the metadata-format decision is step 0, and the 4 skill patches are steps 1–4.

findings.description: The prompt-list behavior (reading IDs from plans/overview-data.js) needs explicit fallback behavior for when the file is absent. Without that, the future implementation may accidentally make an optional metadata field block normal PRD creation in repos without overview-data.js. (This is a refinement of F-002 — F-002 is the design fix; F-010 is the explicit fallback wording.)
findings.suggestedFix: In §3.1, add: 'If plans/overview-data.js (or whatever path the consumer config exposes) is absent or unreadable, the prompt falls back to a free-form string input with a skip option. Never block PRD creation on this lookup.'
